After playing a lot with the plane, Paulo unfolded the sheet and realized that there were several holes in it. How many holes did he count?

method.method_draft: Reverse-unfold the hole location through the pictured sequence. Read the image from right to left: the blue circular hole is on the final folded airplane; each preceding picture shows a fold line by a dotted line. Start with 1 hole mark on the final plane. Undo the last lengthwise fold shown by the vertical dotted line, reflecting the hole to the opposite half, so the count doubles. Then undo the previous side/wing folds indicated by the diagonal dotted fold lines; because the marked point lies in the folded-over wing region, each undoing reflects every current mark into another layer. Continue back through the first top-corner folds shown in the leftmost rectangle. After the three relevant doublings, the unfolded rectangle has 1 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 holes.
